title: Micro-exposure runway and escalation trellis (WIP)
content:
Purpose:
This is a working playbook for small-batch ("micro") exposure runs across Redwood Console / routing layers. The goal is to provide a compact, repeatable runway and an explicit escalation trellis (matrix) for multi-team coordination when rolling out model variants, rerankers, or routing policy changes.

Context / why this is different:
- Many existing rollout docs focus on broad canaries or large A/Bs. Micro-exposure is for: low-risk surface validation, signal extraction for models with low coverage, and quick quality regressions tied to prompt sets.
- Focuses on: short lived slices (minutes->hours), tight telemetry sets, automated guardrails, and human-in-the-loop checkpoints before scaling exposure.

Audience:
- Product PM owning the feature + rollout steward
- Console engineers (routing + feature flags)
- Serving runtime / infra (capacity + fallback variants)
- SRE / oncall owner for the experiment window
- Applied ML / evaluations owner for quality signal monitoring

Quick glossary (for this doc):
- micro-exposure: incremental traffic bursts starting at ~0.01% moving up to 1% in quick steps
- trellis: escalation matrix mapping observed signal breaches to actions/owners
- variant: a model binary or routing policy (e.g., quantized v2, reranker-v3)
- commitment horizon: how long we keep a slice open (default 30m)

Runway template (one-line checklist):
- Define hypothesis + expected metric deltas (latency, cost, quality)
- Pick seed cohort and sampling key (region, customer segment, device)
- Wire telemetry (p50/p95 latency, token-per-request, cost estimate, hallucination score, acceptance rate)
- Create feature-flag slice with TTL and auto-shrink policy
- Dry-run with synthetic traffic (see synth plan below)
- Execute micro-exposure (0.01% -> 0.1% -> 0.5% -> 1%), 2 checkpoints each step
- If all green, promote slice and start stage gating to next channel (canary/A-B)

Signal set (minimum telemetry to observe during micro-exposure):
- Latency: p50, p95, p99 (end-to-end, and model stepwise)
- Cost: estimated tokens * unit cost (per 1k tokens) delta vs baseline
- Quality: prompt-set pass rate (golden prompts), hallucination proxy (excessive out-of-scope entities), rerank precision@k delta
- Stability: rate of model-side errors (500s, OOMs), KV cache hit ratio
- User impact: rejection rate, downstream conversion funnel (if applicable)
- Operational: queue depth, batching efficiency, autoscaler triggers

Escalation trellis (matrix):
- Green: all signals within expected delta -> advance to next exposure step after commitment horizon. Owner: rollout steward.
- Amber-1 (soft degradation): small latency spike (p95 +20%), token cost up to +12%, minor quality regressions (<5% prompt fail). Action: pause automatic step-up, increase synthetic replay and signal sampling, notify infra + ML. Owner: steward + infra oncall.
- Amber-2 (material degradation): p95 +50% or token cost +25% or prompt-fail >10% -> immediate rollback to previous stable variant slice; open PostMortem draft; increase observability retention for the slice. Owner: oncall + steward.
- Red (severe): errors >1% of requests or customer-facing failures/false data -> immediate full rollback, page SRE, initiate incident bridge, stop all further exposure for 24h. Owner: SRE escalation.

Roles & Responsibilities (practical notes):
- Rollout steward (product): owns hypothesis, coordinates rehearsal, approves step-ups.
- Console engineer: creates feature-flag slice, TTL, synthetic traffic route, tagging for telemetry extraction.
- Infra/Serving: pre-warm models, confirm capacity headroom and fallback variants are available.
- Applied ML: provides golden prompt sets, automated eval harness, and a quality threshold.
- SRE/Oncall: monitors ops signals, ready to roll back or mitigate infra faults.
- Comms owner: writes short Slack templates and customer comms if needed.

Rehearsal checklist (pre-run):
- Confirm slice identity + sampling key + expected user IDs (keep seed small)
- Confirm synthetic traffic mirrors real-seed distribution (lengths, tokens, patterns)
- Confirm KV cache seeding plan (if relevant)
- Confirm fallback variant pinned and smoke-tested
- Confirm logging hooks (traces, sample collection, golden prompt attachments)
- Confirm alert thresholds for trellis are wired into experiment dashboard

Synthetic traffic plan (short):
- Start with 10x real-seed RPS for 5 minutes in a private namespace to validate queues
- 60m synthetic replay matching token distribution and heavy tails
- Inject 5% adversarial prompts in a separate tag to estimate hallucination sensitivity

Operational knobs (console + serving):
- Auto-shrink TTL: after X hours without step-up, shrink slice to 0.01%
- Canary fallback policy: prefer cheaper quantized variant when latency breaches, prefer plain rollback when quality breaches
- Emergency kill switch: single endpoint toggled by SRE -> immediate 0% routing to variant across regions

Comms templates (short):
- Slack: "Micro-exposure START: {slice} -> 0.01% for 30m. Steward: @maya, Infra: @luca, ML: @aisha. Watch list: latency p95, prompt-pass. Links: dash / synth logs"
- Pager blurb: "Micro-exposure alert: {metric} breached threshold for {slice}. Action: review and follow trellis. If red, run incident template"

Data capture & artifacts to keep (for PostMortem & model ops):
- Raw request+response samples for failed prompts (sanitized)
- Golden prompt pass/fail log for entire slice window
- Cost trace: per-request token breakdown and runtime breakdown
- Model binary id and config (quantize bits, kernel flags)

Open questions / TODOs (short list):
- How many golden prompts are minimum for statistical confidence at micro exposures? (ML to propose)
- Auto-scaling interaction: should autoscaler be muted during first step-ups to avoid noisy spikes? (infra discussion)
- Hook for customer-facing opt-out: how to route pre-existing customers off slices without biasing metrics?

Immediate next steps (today):
- Set up a rehearsed micro-exposure for reranker-v3 on staging (owner: Luca)
- ML to produce a 50-sample golden prompt set by EOD (owner: Aisha)
- Product to draft hypothesis and commit horizon for the feature (owner: Maya)

Appendix: quick rollback checklist (1-2 lines each)
- Pause step-ups in the console (steward)
- Toggle feature-flag to previous stable variant (console engineer)
- Page SRE if errors > 1% or customer-impacting failures (oncall)
- Capture snapshot: logs, traces, golden prompt failures (ML)
- Short retrospective scheduled within 48h (Product + ML + Infra + SRE)

Notes to self (scratch):
- Try a "paired-slice" pattern where for each micro slice we attach a small synthetic control to offset sampling noise.
- Need an internal dashboard tile that shows delta vs baseline and the trellis state per slice (visual).
